Tier: Tier 1: Overall Process Structure (select exactly one dominant)
Description: Student completes work independently, then uses AI to verify/check/validate the finished work. AI is post-hoc validation, not mid-problem help.
Do NOT apply when: AI is consulted DURING the attempt when the student gets stuck (-> WF02). The student describes repeated attempt-feedback cycles (-> WF04). If both verify-after and help-when-stuck are described, select the one presented as primary and set flag_for_review.
Distinguish from: WF02 (post-hoc checking vs. mid-problem rescue); WF04; WF03 (if the student produces their own solution and compares it to AI-derived steps or equations, the dominant structure is WF01, with WF14/WF10 as Tier 2 steps, NOT WF03)
Example responses: "Solve myself first use AI to check work" • "I usually do the work myself and then use AI to double check it." • "Answer by myself_ Ai to check if im unsure" • "I always do the work on my own, then use AI to check my answers." • "I usually go through the question myself and see if I can derive the equations that it derived" (WF01 dominant + WF10, WF14 in Tier 2)

Tier: Tier 1: Overall Process Structure (select exactly one dominant)
Code: Self-Attempt First; AI Help When Stuck
Description: Student attempts the problem independently FIRST and turns to AI only when stuck, confused, or unable to proceed; AI's role is mid-problem assistance (hints, explanations, next steps), after which the student resumes.
Do NOT apply when: AI's role is checking completed work (-> WF01). The student starts with AI from the outset (-> WF03/WF05). Repeated multi-cycle refinement dominates (-> WF04).
Distinguish from: WF01; WF03; WF04
Example responses: "First I try to solve on my own then ask AI for help when I get stuck or don't know what to do next" • "I attempt every problem myself without use of generative AI. If I am consistently lost or am unable to solve, I turn to AI for assistance." • "I attempt the problem, then use AI for assistance if I am unsure how to continue."

Tier: Tier 1: Overall Process Structure (select exactly one dominant)
Description: Student uses AI in a forward-facing, sequential manner from the outset: AI explains or generates steps and the student learns/works through them in linear progression.
Do NOT apply when: The student attempts independently before involving AI (-> WF01/WF02). The interaction involves cycles of revision and re-prompting (-> WF04). The student takes the answer without working through steps (-> WF05). The student merely REQUESTS steps/formulas within another structure, or produces their own work and compares to AI steps (-> the true dominant Tier 1 code, with WF10 as the Tier 2 step). The student names only a narrow use with no sequential process described (-> WF22).
Distinguish from: WF02; WF04; WF05 (working through steps vs. taking the answer); WF10 (WF03 is the Tier 1 structure when following AI-provided steps IS the workflow from the outset; WF10 is the Tier 2 act of requesting steps and can co-occur with ANY Tier 1 code); WF22
Example responses: "I usually ask the AI the step by step process for the question, I then go through it myself while checking step by step." • "Input the question, follow the steps, and replicate the process myself while referring to class notes"

Tier: Tier 1: Overall Process Structure (select exactly one dominant)
Description: Multiple cycles of attempt-feedback-revision or dialogue-based refinement: the student returns to and revises previous work, or engages in multiple rounds of AI requests/prompt refinement to converge on understanding.
Do NOT apply when: A single consult resolves the issue (-> WF02) or a single linear walkthrough is described (-> WF03).
Distinguish from: WF02; WF03 (cycles vs. one-pass)
Example responses: "I upload the problem I am trying to solve, and then I refine my input to have the software only respond to the specific question I am asking" • "will have a back-and-forth with the AI on how to solve" • "I solve each step myself, and when my answer is different than given, I prompt it with my answer and ask it what is different"

Tier: Tier 1: Overall Process Structure (select exactly one dominant)
Description: Student inputs the problem and takes the AI's answer/solution directly, with no independent attempt, no stepwise working-through, and no iteration described.
Do NOT apply when: The student works through or replicates the AI's steps (-> WF03). Any independent attempt precedes AI use (-> WF01/WF02).
Distinguish from: WF03 (taking output vs. learning through steps)
Example responses: "I copy and paste problems and send them through AI to solve it and show me the steps in detail." • "screenshot and then paste" • "I submit the question into the AI and ask for how to solve it."

Tier: Tier 1: Overall Process Structure (select exactly one dominant)
Description: Explicit statement that the student does not use AI for this course, or does not attempt to. STANDALONE: select no Tier 2 codes (exception: WF18/WF19 may be applied when a limitation or distrust is stated as the reason for non-use).
Do NOT apply when: The student uses AI rarely but describes a workflow for when they do (code that workflow).
Distinguish from: WF08 (an explicit non-use statement is codable, not noise)
Example responses: "I don't use AI for this class." • "I didn't use AI" • "I never use AI." • "I found that LLMs were incapable of understanding the geometry of questions... For this reason I avoided using them" (WF06 + WF18 + WF19)

Tier: Tier 1: Overall Process Structure (select exactly one dominant)
Description: Student names only a narrow, specific use of AI (e.g., concept reminders, debugging code, formula lookup) WITHOUT describing any sequential process from question to answer. The response describes what AI is for, not a workflow. Co-code the matching Tier 2 codes (often WF09, WF17).
Do NOT apply when: Any sequential process is described, however brief (-> WF01-WF05). The student states they do not use AI (-> WF06).
Distinguish from: WF03 (no step sequence described vs. following steps as the workflow); WF06 (narrow use vs. no use); WF07 (a nameable single-purpose use vs. an unclassifiable process)
Example responses: "So far I have only used them to help remind me of concepts from previous physics classes." • "Only used to debug matlab code. Sucks theoretical."

Tier: Tier 1: Overall Process Structure (select exactly one dominant)
Description: A codable overall process structure is described but none of WF01-WF06 fits. Describe the structure in the notes field.
Do NOT apply when: Any of WF01-WF06 or WF22 fits, even at low confidence (apply it and flag instead). The student names only a narrow, single-purpose use with no process described (-> WF22).
Distinguish from: WF01-WF06, WF22 (residual only)
Example responses: (residual; describe in notes)

Tier: Tier 1: Overall Process Structure (select exactly one dominant)
Description: Responses that provide no codable data: 'N/A', blank, nonsensical, or failing to address the prompt. STANDALONE: select no Tier 2 codes.
Do NOT apply when: Any other Tier 1 code can be applied, even at low confidence (apply it and flag instead).
Distinguish from: WF06 (no codable content vs. explicit non-use)
Example responses: "c" • "no" • "Solve along" • "The process in solving the questions"

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student asks AI to explain concepts, theories, underlying principles, or abstract ideas: breaking down complex topics, simplifying, or clarifying examples. Focus on deepening comprehension of WHAT and WHY.
Do NOT apply when: The request is for HOW-to procedures, formulas, or sequential solution steps (-> WF10).
Distinguish from: WF10 (what/why vs. how); WF12 (explanation vs. hints toward an answer)
Example responses: "I only ask it to explain a topic for me" • "I usually have it explain concepts" • "I use AI to explain or expand on a problem/concept if I don't understand where to start."

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student asks AI for step-by-step procedures, equations, formulas, algorithms, methods, or sequential solutions: HOW to execute a process.
Do NOT apply when: The request is for conceptual understanding (-> WF09) or for hints/partial guidance rather than the full procedure (-> WF12).
Distinguish from: WF09; WF12; Tier 1 WF03 (WF10 marks the request itself, at the step level, and co-occurs with any Tier 1 structure; it does not imply the workflow is AI-guided)
Example responses: "Ask it to lay down the stpes and equations" • "I usually just ask it for formulas, never to solve actual problems" • "Ask it to generate a list of steps to take to approach a problem"

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student uses AI to memorize, internalize, drill, or practice procedures: flashcards, generated practice problems, quizzing, repetition toward fluency.
Do NOT apply when: A procedure is requested once to solve a specific problem (-> WF10).
Distinguish from: WF10 (drilling for fluency vs. one-time how-to)
Example responses: "The process of how to solve and memorize the steps simply." • "ask AI to generate a synopsis review of the topic, and to occasionally generate practice problems or example problems for me to review" • "ask AI for similar but different [problems]"

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student asks AI for hints, guiding questions, leading prompts, or partial guidance rather than direct answers or full solutions; Socratic-style interaction intended to prompt thinking.
Do NOT apply when: The full procedure or solution is requested (-> WF10). The student describes constraining the prompt as a tactic without a hint-seeking goal (-> WF20; the two frequently co-occur; apply both when hints are sought via explicit constraints).
Distinguish from: WF10; WF20 (pedagogical goal vs. prompt tactic)
Example responses: "I would usually tell AI to give me hints to help me get started with the question." • "not giving me the answers, but asking me at each point what I think the next step should be." • "Usually ask for hints but not for answers"

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student checks whether their FINAL answer or result is correct by comparing to AI's answer or having AI verify it. Quick 'is this right?' on the end product, not the process.
Do NOT apply when: Steps/methodology are compared, not just the final answer (-> WF14). The student asks AI to diagnose WHY they were wrong (-> WF15).
Distinguish from: WF14 (final answer vs. step comparison); WF15
Example responses: "I only use AI tools to check my final answer if used." • "I also then compare my final answer to the AI answer." • "Checking FBD or checking only my final answer with it"

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student solves independently, then reviews the AI's step-by-step solution to compare reasoning/methodology, examining HOW each step was done and where they match or differ.
Do NOT apply when: Only the final answer is compared (-> WF13). The AI is asked to find/explain the student's error (-> WF15).
Distinguish from: WF13; WF15 (student compares vs. AI diagnoses)
Example responses: "I go through its thinking process and compare it with my own." • "Do a hwk problem by myself, ask an ai engine to do the problem, compare answers and ask if anything doesn't match" • "I usually attempt a problem and then run it through AI to see if we agree on the steps to solve."

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student asks AI to identify and explain how and why errors occurred in the STUDENT'S work: root-cause analysis, debugging, locating where logic broke down.
Do NOT apply when: The student locates differences themselves by comparison (-> WF14) or only checks whether the answer is right (-> WF13).
Distinguish from: WF13; WF14
Example responses: "I'll ask the AI to look at my work and point out where the mistake is" • "I usually use it to find errors in my process when solving a question and getting it wrong." • "i take a photo of it and ask chat what I might have done wrong"

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student verifies correctness by comparing AI output against external authoritative sources: textbook, lecture notes, posted solutions, class problems. Do NOT apply when: Verification is against the student's own work (-> WF13/WF14).
Distinguish from: WF13/WF14 (external source vs. own work)
Example responses: "once I think through its answer I often verify with the textbook and my own understanding" • "I then would see if AI answer was correct by comparing them to in class problems"

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student explicitly describes conditions, boundaries, or contexts under which they use AI differently: only for certain topics, task types, or situations.
Do NOT apply when: The condition is simply 'when stuck' (that is Tier 1 WF02, not a Tier 2 step).
Distinguish from: Tier 1 WF02 (topic/task boundaries vs. attempt-first fallback)
Example responses: "Only used to debu[g] matlab code. Sucks theoretical." • "I rarely use AI for this course since most have issues with diagrams. I primarily use it for explaining concepts"

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student describes AI's inability or limitations in interpreting diagrams, schematics, images, or geometry, including workarounds (describing the figure in words, verifying the AI's reading of the figure).
Do NOT apply when: General distrust is expressed without reference to visual/diagram content (-> WF19).

Example responses: "figure out how to turn the image into words cause the ai struggles reading images but it understands words" • "LLMs were incapable of understanding the geometry of questions" • "ask it to explain what it is seeing so I know it's interpreting the problem correctly"

Description: Student expresses doubt, caution, or distrust about the reliability of AI outputs, including mentions of hallucination or frequent errors.
Do NOT apply when: The doubt is specifically about diagram/visual interpretation (-> WF18; apply both when both general and visual distrust appear).

Tier: Tier 2: Specific Process Steps (select all that apply)
Description: Student describes deliberately structuring or constraining prompts: withholding the answer request, instructing AI not to solve fully, specifying context/topic, isolating a sub-question, or refining inputs to control output.
Do NOT apply when: The prompt tactic is not described (a plain 'I ask it to explain' is WF09/WF10, not WF20).

Example responses: "I tell AI to not solve everything" • "I make sure it doesn't give me the answer but how to start the problem" • "specify to the LLM that I want to walk through the task rather than receive an immediate answer" • "prompt the AI by telling it what topic the problem belongs to"
